Q: Not able to generate oauth.json for ytmusicapi in python A:

You have created an OAuth client of the Desktop type, and the current ytmusicapi documentation for OAuth directly requires OAuth client ID → TVs and Limited Input devices and states that this OAuth flow uses the TV device flow.

Q: Is there a better way to make a pie-donut plot using ggplot? A: 
``` r
library(ggplot2)
library(geomtextpath)
library(ggnewscale)
library(tibble)

tribble(
  ~Expression, ~Substrate, ~Emin, ~Emax, ~Smin, ~Smax,
  "Down-reg",  "Acetate",  0, .5, 0, .25,
  "Down-reg",  "Fructan",  0,  .5, .25, .5,
  "Up-reg",    "Benzoate", .5, 1, .5,  .75,
  "Up-reg",    "Glucose",  .5, 1, .75,  1,
) |> 
  ggplot()+
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(-1, 4))+
  coord_polar(theta = "y")+
  geom_rect(
    aes(
      xmin = 1, 
      xmax = 2,
      ymin = Emin,
      ymax = Emax,
      fill = Expression
      ), 
    alpha = .5) +
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
    "Down-reg" = "#cd9900",
    "Up-reg" = "#00817e")
  )+
  ggnewscale::new_scale_fill() +
  geom_rect(
  aes(
    xmin = 2, 
    xmax = 3,
    ymin = Smin,
    ymax = Smax,
    fill = Substrate
  ), 
  color = "#ffffff",
  alpha = .25)+
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c(
      "Acetate" = "#cdbc00",
      "Fructan" = "#cd7800",
      "Benzoate" = "#00816c",
      "Glucose" = "#006c81"
    )
  ) +
  geom_textpath(aes(x = 1.5, y = (Emin+Emax)/2, label = Expression), angle = 90)+
  geom_textpath(aes(x = 2.5, y = (Smin+Smax)/2, label = Substrate), angle = 90)+
  theme_void()

Created on 2025-10-07 with reprex v2.1.1

Q: Why does ggplot legend not display some categories when color is mapped conditionally? A:

Try wrapping the ifelse() for color and shape in a factor() function and explicitly setting the levels of those factors. I also added show.legend = TRUE to geom_point() and drop = FALSE to scale_color_manual() and scale_shape_manual().

I had to remove the position argument from geom_errorbarh() because it referred to pd, which I don't have.

ggplot(df, aes(x = estimate, y = moderator,
               color = factor(ifelse(p_value > 0.10, "gray50", outcome), 
                              levels = c("gray50", "out1", "out2", "out3", "out4")),
               shape = factor(ifelse(p_value > 0.10, "gray50", outcome), 
                              levels = c("gray50", "out1", "out2", "out3", "out4")),
               alpha = ifelse(p_value <= 0.05, 1,
                              ifelse(p_value <= 0.10, 0.5, 0.3)),
               group = outcome)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = ci_lo, xmax = ci_hi),
                 height = 0) +   
  geom_point(size = 2.5, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), show.legend = TRUE) +
  facet_grid(~ treatment) +
  scale_color_manual(drop = FALSE,
    values = c(out1 = "red", out2 = "orange",
               out3 = "blue", out4 = "green",
               gray50 = "gray50"),
    breaks = c("out1","out2","out3","out4"),
    name = "Outcome") +
  scale_shape_manual(drop = FALSE,
    values = c(out1 = 17, out2 = 16,
               out3 = 17, out4 = 16,
               gray50 = 4),
    breaks = c("out1","out2","out3","out4"),
    name = "Outcome") +
  scale_alpha_identity() +
  theme_classic()

Q: Adding geom_text in patchwork with shared y-axis and both positive and negative values A:

Don't use a factor for Herkunftsschulform and use position stack to reverse the order for the fill:

data_schule_schulform$Herkunftsschulform <- as.character(data_schule_schulform$Herkunftsschulform)
ggplot() +
  geom_col(
    data = data_schule_schulform,
    aes(fill = Herkunftsschulform, y = Anzahl, x = Schuljahr),
    position = position_stack(reverse = TRUE)
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = data_schule_schulform,
    aes (
      label = Herkunftsschulform, 
      y = Anzahl, 
      x = Schuljahr,
      group = Schuljahr
      ),
    position = position_stack(vjust = .5, reverse = FALSE)

Q: Trying to plot a R grouped bar plot with one color condition on ggplot A:

Not sure if this is what you're looking for, but if you 'fill' by type you can get coloured bars, e.g.

library(tidyverse)

df <- data.frame(Year = rep(2000:2023, each = 13),
                 season = c("DJF", "JFM", "FMA", "MAM", "AMJ", "MJJ", "JJA", "JAS", "ASO", "SON", "OND", "NDJ"),
                 Value = sin(runif(312)) - 0.5)
df %>%
  mutate(type = if_else(Value < 0, "negative", "positive"),
         season = factor(season, levels = c("DJF", "JFM", "FMA", "MAM", "AMJ", "MJJ", "JJA", "JAS", "ASO", "SON", "OND", "NDJ"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = Value, group = season, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("positive" = "firebrick3",
                               "negative" = "dodgerblue"))

But then the season information is obfuscated... Perhaps facetting the data would be better? E.g.

df %>%
  mutate(type = if_else(Value < 0, "negative", "positive"),
         season = factor(season, levels = c("DJF", "JFM", "FMA", "MAM", "AMJ", "MJJ", "JJA", "JAS", "ASO", "SON", "OND", "NDJ"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = Value, group = season, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("positive" = "firebrick3",
                               "negative" = "dodgerblue")) +
  facet_wrap(~season, ncol = 1)

Or making a grid?

df %>%
  mutate(type = if_else(Value < 0, "negative", "positive"),
         season = factor(season, levels = c("DJF", "JFM", "FMA", "MAM", "AMJ", "MJJ", "JJA", "JAS", "ASO", "SON", "OND", "NDJ"))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = Year, y = Value, group = season, fill = type)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("positive" = "firebrick3",
                               "negative" = "dodgerblue")) +
  facet_grid(vars(season), vars(Year), scales = "free_x")

Do any of these approaches solve your problem?

Q: Arrow tips overlap with geom_node_label() in ggraph — how to stop arrows at label border? A:

Try replacing circle() end cap with label_rect().

Q: Showing observed data on x-axis of ggolot A:

Without any data it is a bit difficult to tell what is going on but here are a few solutions that might help you/push you in the right direction.

  1. Would simply adding geom_point() rather than using geom_point() with WeekFreq help? It would show the raw data points. IT would not be very readable if there's a lot of data and overplotting.

For the other solutions I simulated some dummy data to have something to work with (I made continuous x rather than date but it should not change anything)

set.seed(2137)
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
# dummy data
x <- rnorm(100, 0 , .5) |> round(1)
year = rep(c(1,2), 100)
y <- .3 + sin(x^2) - .5*cos(x^3) + rnorm(1000, 0, .6)
dummy_df <- data.frame(x, y, year)

dummy_freq <- dummy_df |>
  count(year, x, name = "n_x")
  1. You could use geom_count(): It adds dots proportional to number of observations + I am placing them at different y to avoid overplotting both years. You'd have to adjust the y level to fit your plot. I like this one best
dummy_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_smooth() +
  geom_count(aes(x = x, y = ifelse(year == 1,-.5, -.3), color = factor(year)), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  theme(axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"), plot.title = element_text(size = 24),
        axis.text=element_text(size=18),axis.title=element_text(size=22,face="bold"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), legend.position = 'none')
  1. Using geom_rug(): It'ss give you a similar solution to what you have with geom_point()
dummy_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_smooth() +
  geom_rug(aes(color = factor(year)), sides = "b", length = unit(10, "pt"))+
  theme(axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"), plot.title = element_text(size = 24),
        axis.text=element_text(size=18),axis.title=element_text(size=22,face="bold"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), legend.position = 'none')
  1. Using geom_segment(): You could also try to plot lines with length proportional to number of observations. OVerplotting is dealt with with slight shift on x axis. You might have to adjust the y and yend aesthetics to fit your plot as well as how n_x is scaled here.
dummy_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = x, y = y)) +
  geom_smooth() +
  geom_segment(data = dummy_freq, aes(x = ifelse(year == 1, x, x + .02), xend = ifelse(year == 1, x, x + .02), y = -.7, yend= -.7 + n_x/100, color = factor(year)), inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  theme(axis.line = element_line(colour = "black"), plot.title = element_text(size = 24),
        axis.text=element_text(size=18),axis.title=element_text(size=22,face="bold"),
        panel.grid = element_blank(), axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, vjust = 1),
        axis.title.x = element_blank(), legend.position = 'none')

The problem with geom_dotplot() will be that even if you add it to your plot it will start at 0 which is in the middle of your plot.

Q: Is combining corrplots possible using patchwork? A:

Looks like this can’t be done. However, the {ggcorrplot} package was designed to mimic corrplot with the same formatting options. Those plots could then be stacked with {patchwork}.
